subject: general
question: For completely randomised design for k treatments and n observation, yᵢj = response from the jth unit receiving ith treatment, {sum _i}{sum _j}{yᵢj} = y and sum _j{ⁿ_i}{yᵢj} = {y_i} . Which of the following options is correct?

options.text: sum ᵢ ₌ ₁^ksum j ₌ ₁{ⁿ_i}{({yᵢj} - {overline y _i})²} represents sum of squares of due to error
sum ᵢ ₌ ₁^k{({overline y ᵢ.} - overline y )²} represents sum of squares due to treatments
sum ᵢ ₌ ₁^ksum j ₌ ₁{ⁿ_i}{({yᵢj} - {overline y _i})²} represents total sum of squares
sum ᵢ ₌ ₁^k{n_i({overline y ᵢ.} - overline y )²} represents sum of squares due to treatments

solution:
The correct answer is: sumᵢ₌₁^k({overline y ᵢ.} - overline y )² represents the sum of squares due to treatments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a completely randomized design, **y****ᵢ**j represents the response from the jth unit receiving the ith treatment.
 
• The symbol "Σ" represents the sum of all observations.
 
• The expression sum j{ⁿ_i}{y{ij}} = {y_i} represents the sum of the responses for a specific treatment (i) and is equal to the mean response for that treatment (overline y ᵢ.).
 
• The expression sum ᵢ ₌ ₁^k{({overline y ᵢ.} - overline y )²} represents the sum of squares due to treatments, which is a measure of the variation in the response variable that can be attributed to the different treatments. This expression calculates the difference between the mean response for each treatment (\overline y _{i.}) and the overall mean response (\overline y), squares these differences, and then sums these squared differences across all treatments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The sum of squares due to treatments is used in the **analysis of variance (ANOVA)** to determine if there are significant differences in the response variable between the different treatments.
 
• The sum of squares due to treatments is just one component of the total sum of squares, which represents the total variation in the response variable.
 
• Understanding the concept of sum of squares and its use in ANOVA is important for conducting and interpreting experiments involving treatment comparisons.
 
• It is important to have a clear understanding of the experimental design and the data collection process in order to accurately interpret the results of an ANOVA.
